articles.title: Zero-Downtime GraphQL Evolution in GitLab: Fixing Multi-Node Upgrades with @gl_introduced
articles.excerpt: A deep dive into GraphQL schema evolution, rolling deployments, mixed-version infrastructure, and backward-compatible frontend queries. Distributed applications rarely upgrade every server instance si…
articles.body: A deep dive into GraphQL schema evolution, rolling deployments, mixed-version infrastructure, and backward-compatible frontend queries. Distributed applications rarely upgrade every server instance simultaneously. In a multi-node deployment, different application versions can temporarily coexist while a rolling upgrade is in progress. This creates an important compatibility challenge: frontend assets served by a newer application version may send GraphQL requests to an older backend node that does not yet understand the updated schema. This is not simply a deployment sequencing problem. It is a contract compatibility problem between independently deployed frontend and backend components.
articles.author: Manish Kumar

articles.title: Invoicing On Site: What Works When There's No Signal and the Client Pays in Another Currency
articles.excerpt: The mechanical room is two floors below street level, behind a fire door, and has no bars. You have finished the repair. The building manager is standing there with his keys out, ready to sign off and…
articles.body: The mechanical room is two floors below street level, behind a fire door, and has no bars. You have finished the repair. The building manager is standing there with his keys out, ready to sign off and go home, and he says the thing that decides whether you get paid this month: "Can you leave me the invoice?" At a desk, that is a two-minute task. In a basement, on a phone, with wet gloves and 12% battery, it is a different problem — the part of invoicing desktop software never solved, and the reason so many field service businesses bill a week late. Not from laziness. From physics. This guide covers three things that make field invoicing work: billing on site, what "offline" really means, and how to handle clients who pay in a currency you do not live in.
articles.author: Karactif Tech

articles.title: Invoicing for Photographers and Creatives: Price the Work, Then Bill for the Rights
articles.excerpt: The gallery goes out on Tuesday. The invoice goes out on Wednesday. Three weeks later the client replies: "Loved the shots — we're also going to use a couple in the spring campaign, and the printer ne…
articles.body: The gallery goes out on Tuesday. The invoice goes out on Wednesday. Three weeks later the client replies: "Loved the shots — we're also going to use a couple in the spring campaign, and the printer needs a high-res file for the billboard." And now you are having a conversation about usage rights that should have been settled before the first frame was taken. The images were licensed for a website refresh. Nothing on the invoice said so. In the client's mind, they bought the photos. This is the most expensive gap in creative work, and it is not a photography problem — it is an invoicing problem. A creative invoice is not just a payment request. It is the plain-language record of what the client bought, what they may do with it, and when the balance is due.
articles.author: Karactif Tech

articles.title: HackProof: catch missing pieces in your hackathon write-up
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the MLH × DEV Writing Challenge. A hackathon project can be almost finished and still be difficult to share. The demo link may be missing, a template placeholder may still be…
articles.body: This is a submission for the MLH × DEV Writing Challenge . What I Built A hackathon project can be almost finished and still be difficult to share. The demo link may be missing, a template placeholder may still be in the draft, or a paragraph may describe a claim without pointing to anything that supports it. I built HackProof , a small offline command-line tool to catch some of those gaps before publishing. Give it a DEV-style Markdown post and HackProof checks for a title, the mlhacks tag, the four sections in the official challenge template, a demo URL, and obvious draft markers such as an empty title or bracketed fill-in instructions. It can print a text summary, produce JSON for automation, or create a standalone HTML report.
articles.author: SAIF MODAN

articles.title: Building a Resilient B2B Email Marketing CRM Using n8n, LangChain, and OpenRouter
articles.excerpt: How to split AI content generation from transactional mailing to prevent spam, ensure strict JSON outputs, and keep API costs low. When building B2B outreach automation, combining AI generation and em…
articles.body: How to split AI content generation from transactional mailing to prevent spam, ensure strict JSON outputs, and keep API costs low. When building B2B outreach automation, combining AI generation and email dispatch into a single linear workflow is a recipe for disaster. If the AI you are using hallucinates, outputs malformed text, or triggers a rate limit, the entire execution fails, or even worse, sends an incorrect email to a client. This guide focuses on how to solve this by designing a Two-Step architecture using n8n, LangChain, and OpenRouter (Claude), integrated with a clean database layer. The Core Challenge Standard email automation tools lack intelligent contextual personalization, while raw LLM implementations are unpredictable.
articles.author: Emiliano Allende

articles.title: Can't Top Up a DeepSeek API Key From Your Country? Every Workaround, Compared Honestly
articles.excerpt: If you've tried to use the DeepSeek API from Nigeria, Pakistan, Vietnam, parts of India, or a long list of other countries, you already know the wall: the model is cheap, the docs are fine, your code…
articles.body: If you've tried to use the DeepSeek API from Nigeria, Pakistan, Vietnam, parts of India, or a long list of other countries, you already know the wall: the model is cheap, the docs are fine, your code works — and then the top-up page rejects your card. The API itself isn't geo-blocked for most people. The payment rail is. This is the most common problem I hear from developers outside the US/EU/China payment systems, so here is every workaround I know of, with the trade-offs stated plainly. Option 1: Get a card that works Virtual dollar cards (issued by local fintechs in many countries) are the most common fix. When they work, this is the cleanest path: you keep a direct account with DeepSeek, you pay the official price, nobody sits in the middle. The catch is reliability.

articles.title: It's Always DNS: I Started Turning Incident-Channel Jokes Into T-Shirts
articles.excerpt: Hey dev.to. First post here, so a quick intro: I work in tech, and for years my favourite writing has not been documentation. It has been the incident channel. If you have ever been on a 2 a.m. call,…
articles.body: Hey dev.to. First post here, so a quick intro: I work in tech, and for years my favourite writing has not been documentation. It has been the incident channel. If you have ever been on a 2 a.m. call, you know the lines. They are short, they are true, and everybody on the call understands them instantly: "It's always DNS." "MFA is my love language." "Human in the loop." "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" (The eternal classic.) A few weeks ago I started turning those lines into designs, mostly to see if I could. That experiment now has a name, Compile & Cotton, and a small shop of wearable inside jokes for people who build the internet. How it actually works People ask about the mechanics, so here is the honest version: The lines come first.

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.title: 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab has raised the launch cost of its next-gen Neutron rocket by more than 25%, an increase that reflects high demand amid a looming liftoff bottleneck.
articles.body: The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call.

M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus.

articles.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
articles.excerpt: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility.
articles.body: A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum.
